newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs up by noon, aided by Tokyo stocks.
newsitem.headline: JGBs up by noon, aided by Tokyo stocks.

text.p: Cash and futures Japanese government bonds (JGBs) rose by Tokyo midday on Wednesday, aided by Japan's main stock index's fall through the key psychological support of 20,000, traders said.
The key September was at 124.60 at noon, up from 124.36 on Tuesday. The yield of the benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB was at 2.310 percent, down from Tuesday's 2.320 percent.
The Trust Fund Bureau of the Ministry of Finance offered to buy 100 billion yen in long-term bonds outright at 0110 GMT.
The bureau's buying cheered up the market, inducing buying of fixed interest rates in the swap market, traders said.
The Bank of Japan showed an accomodative stance, via letting the market have a surplus of 400 billion yen for the second day in a row.
"Stock's decline along with monetary authorities' generous credit stance underscored the bullish bond sentiment," said a city bank trader.
At midday, the Nikkei 225 was down 183.92 points or 0.91 percent at 19,991.60. Its September futures shed 60 to 20,040.
Some said that public funds sold two-year JGBs for five-year JGBs in a bid to reshuffle their portfolio.
